text:
Maya Chen: Quick q — the Console cost-preview slider for rollouts: is that showing marginal per-invocation delta when routing switches models, or the amortized + cache-warmup impact? the canary numbers looked way lower than the billing sim 😕
Samir Patel: It should be amortized across a 24h warmup window by default. Marginal mode exists but we hid it behind the API flag. can you link the rollout where you saw the mismatch? :thinking:
Maya Chen: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/PR-4823 — canary route moved traffic to small-quantized variant. Console preview said -18% cost, billing sim +3%. Screenshot: "[img]"
Oliver King: Likely cache-warmup modeling mismatch. Console is applying our "fast-warmup" heuristic for KV cache hits, billing sim runs a conservative cold-start profile. We exposed two knobs in the preview API: mode: amortized|marginal and cache_profile: fast|conservative|observed. Example:
POST /api/cost_preview
{
  "route":"canary-a",
  "mode":"marginal",
  "cache_profile":"observed"
}
Gina R.: Also check telemetry sample-rate. If the billing sim ingests sampled token traces at 1% but the preview uses full synthetic traces, the unit costs will swing. We should surface sample-rate impact in the UI.
Samir Patel: Agree. Product question: default UX should avoid surprising teams. I vote default to amortized+conservative cache_profile and a tooltip: "why numbers differ from billing" linking to docs. Option to toggle marginal/more aggressive profiles. :+1:
Maya Chen: That sounds safe. For the canary owner, would toggling to marginal + fast reproduce the console delta? (want to debug quickly)
Oliver King: Yes, try mode: marginal and cache_profile: fast — that'll remove amortization and assume warmed KV cache. If that matches the +3% you saw, then the discrepancy is pure warmup assumption.
Maya Chen: Trying now... (posted results) — switching to marginal/fast yields +2.8% which aligns with billing sim. Thanks. 😌
Samir Patel: Follow-ups: 1) add sample-rate badge in preview; 2) expose the two API knobs in Console advanced settings; 3) add a small in-Console explanation of the default 24h amortization window and how it affects savings.
Gina R.: I'll file the telemetry task — sampled token alignment and add a unit-test that runs preview API with sampled traces to ensure parity.
deploy-bot: New PR created: https://redwood.internal/pulls/4891 — "console: cost-preview defaults & advanced knobs" by Gina R.
Maya Chen: Cool. One more ask — can we keep a subtle warning when teams run rollout preview with non-default profiles like marginal/fast? We don't want folks to ship based on a best-case assumption.
Samir Patel: Good call — confirm we'll show a red banner if mode==marginal || cache_profile==fast saying "Estimated values exclude amortization and assume warmed caches".
Oliver King: I'll add the banner and wire up the API. Gina pls add the sampling test and I'll pair on the UI copy.
Gina R.: On it. Filing follow-up issues and linking to PR. :thumbsup:
